items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Speaking of tenor-players, there a, was another tenor player, Dick Wilson, out of Andy Kirk's Band. But he -- you could barely hear him.

ctx.x: And where was it that you met him?

Here in Los Angeles, when they came out here. And this was a say around '37. When they made "Swinging the Blues" and "Taxi War Dance", "Every Tub", "Sent for you Yesterday and Here you come Today"; everything they did was good. "Rock-a-bye Basie", you know. And then later on, "The World is Mad", "Harvard Blues", did you ever hear Don Byas play the Harvard Blues with Basie? (Whistle). He told a beautiful story on that. But the band, the reed section was like Lester Young and Herschel Evans. Now Herschel Evans took…

Seattle, Washington. And his mother died and that was his only living relative and when she died and left everything to him. He went bananas. He just went out to lunch. It was a long time before he rejoined Kirk. Then when he did join Kirk, he turned Alcoholic(?) alcoholic, drug addict, you name it, whatever you had to offer, he wanted some of it.
